title: Shared rules for all housing help
parameters: Income, income lines, immigrant eligibility, verification, conditions and residency, kept in one place; no work or treatment condition; no residency rules; mixed-status families keep prorated help indefinitely, with the right not to contend status, written into Section 214; HUD's February 2026 proposed rule withdrawn or rescinded
eligibility: All households under HOU-4, HOU-4A, HOU-4D, HOU-1D

definitions; disapplies 42 U.S.C. 1437j(c) to new awards
restated as conditions on new money

title: One rental help system (guarantee, vouchers, emergency help harmonized)
parameters: Common application, shared access points, one household record, income found once reused for 12 months, defined hand-offs; consent-based record sharing until the regular bill passes; the record holds only basic information collected for everyone, no citizenship or immigration status (status findings stay with the housing agency: proposed, for Espen); statutory bar on use or sharing for immigration enforcement, with penalties (taxpayer-information model proposed, for Espen); R1 readiness tranche (proposed $0.75B, range $0.5-1B)
eligibility: Applicants to HOU-1D, HOU-4A, HOU-4D, HOU-4.08

title: Order of reach
parameters: Stage 1 people with no home of their own: literally homeless, and families with children doubled up, shown by their own word or a school record, no deadline test and no cap; order by local need-based intake, counts published yearly, a two-year imbalance triggers review (DEC-2026-11-09-12); stage 2 ELI families with children with severe problems; stage 3 disabled ELI renters from 2038; within stage: severity, youngest children, date; older non-disabled renters reconsidered once the care program is scoped
eligibility: As stated; local preferences allowed, no residency rules

parameters: Tight market: vacancy <=4% two years or <50% lease-up in 180 days (judgment); 2030-31 vouchers everywhere; from 2032 up to 25% attached in tight markets, max 50% after evaluation; move with a voucher after 12 months, funded from the household's own award; no attached awards in tracts over 30% poverty; randomized evaluation by 2036
eligibility: New awards under HOU-4A and HOU-4D

parameters: Named navigator offered; contact expected at least monthly; provider follows a set re-engagement protocol; non-engagement never ends lease, subsidy or place; amend 24 CFR 578.75(h) and HUD-VASH (automatic move to a regular voucher); providers offer or connect to medicines for opioid use disorder, naloxone, contingency management, ACT; priority for highest-use chronically homeless people; report contact, retention, overdose deaths, medicine starts, exits; restore the CoC permanent housing priority; tenants enforce the lease protection with a private right of action and attorney's fees
